messages:
Maya: quick follow-up from the admission surface chat. i hacked a lightweight 'fast-admit' shim that returns a tiny admit code so runtime doesn't wait on heavy policy checks. thoughts?  

Arjun: sounds promising. paste the API sketch and the expected p95/p99 targets.

Maya: sketch: runtime sends compact envelope, proxy replies with admit enum + optional action hint. heavy policy runs out-of-band and can issue later revoke or downgrade events. keeps hot path <1ms ideally.

Liz: admit enum + hint ok. how do we express partial allow (eg allow but rate-limit more aggressively)? hint?

Maya: yes hint vals like "allow", "degraded-slim", "deny" or "apply-rate:0.5". proto will encode numeric params for rate modifiers.

Sam: example envelope?

Maya: ```
{
  token: "t-9x7",
  tenant: "team-orchid",
  units: 120,
  trace_id: "rid-..."
}
```
response: `{ admit: 0|1|2, hint: "degraded-slim" }`

Julia: major concerns: 1) bookkeeping when policy revokes after admit, 2) billing accuracy, 3) observable lineage for audits.

Arjun: agree. runtime must attach lineage id to requests and persist admit decisions short-term so revokes can be applied. we should avoid blocking on policy but still be able to retract.

Maya: implementation idea: proxy writes admission events to a compacted topic (admit-state) and revocation events to an event topic. runtime sidecar subscribes and reconciles local session state.

Liz: deployment: central pool vs per-node sidecar? tradeoffs?

Maya: central pool simpler ops but adds cross-AZ latency. sidecar reduces latency and gives locality to KV caching but increases per-node footprint. recommend sidecar for high-throughput clusters, central for small regions.

Sam: ownership and versioning: runtime defines wire proto. security defines scoring and hint semantics. need clear compatibility rules.

Julia: also need tenant-level fail-open policy. for some customers fail-open allowed, for others we must fail-closed. store in tenant metadata service.

Arjun: failure scenarios: if proxy unreachable, sidecar should consult cached admits and fall back per-tenant rule. if policy service fails, revocations will just stop (monitoring alert).

Maya: revocation handling options we discussed: immediate session termination, stop persisting KV state for that session, or reroute to a fallback model. add flags to hint to indicate recommended remediation.

Liz: telemetry: add X-RW-Lineage header carrying a UUID. emit to traces, metrics, logs, and billing pipeline so reconciler can link events.

Sam: billing: when revoke happens after tokens consumed, finance needs a reconciliation hook. propose emitting a settle-event to billing with original admit + final outcome. we should also tag suspected false-positives.

Maya: will add settle event to the event stream. runtime will mark outcome and billing will consume.

Julia: policy pushes could trigger mass revokes. need backpressure on policy stream. implement rate-limited delta pushes and a breaker on the proxy to reject bursts, with a retry backoff from policy side.

Arjun: can we have incremental diffs by tenant rather than global rule pushes? that will reduce blast radius.

Maya: yes policy service will support per-tenant deltas and bulk mode for emergencies (with special admin flag).

infra-bot: canary created: admit-sidecar:v1 deployed -> 8 pods (us-east-1).

Sam: rollout plan: locally in canary cluster -> small internal tenants -> opt-in external customers -> broad. monitor p95 latency, revoke-rate, false-positive alerts, billing-reconciliations/time-to-settle.

Liz: i'll pick up the sidecar implementation. spec: expose small gRPC endpoint, use proto v1, support local cache and subscribe to admit-state topic.

Maya: i'll write the RFC with diagrams and a failure-mode matrix. call out: wire proto, hint taxonomy, tenant fail-open flag, revocation event schema, telemetry fields, and rollout plan.

Sam: i'll own runtime subscriber and billing hooks. Julia/security will own policy scoring and the revocation decisioning model.

Julia: noted. will prepare a brief on expected FP/TP behavior and thresholds for automatic revokes vs review.

Maya: thanks everyone. i'll post the RFC this afternoon and add owners to the doc. tagging @Liz @Sam @Julia for visibility.

infra-bot: reminder: proto schema freeze in 4h. file a change request if you edit the admit proto.
